name: Guardian cryptic crossword, Penguin book 11 No 59

clue.text: Decided during a trial to be accomplished
The girl-friend (perhaps Alma, the Italian one) is back
Sounding, in the main, to have given old copper for new jelly
After a sideshoot dispensed with Scarface?
Turbulent as one Norman state
The panpsychist is back in a fog
First-footing boss-lady had no right to begin 8
Takes in Roman: he is in a bed-sit
There’s rubbish in the entry throttle
Invalid carriage for a healer, you said, with one arm
Jog to the first swim on the south coast
Said to have let be the small fry
The essential part is to be a reformed, sinless, intransigent
Cooling-off process needed if a feminist works in the allot- ment
A narrow escape from frozen earth in Greenland
The flower that’s said to make noses wrinkle
Vans of this type ain’t half strong!
The constant application of a tourniquet
A left-wing teacher lost his head on a carving stone
The Medici’s brother Filippo sounds saucy!
At a drill ordered in Bible on the potter’s field
The first of 8 reckons to take a metre to change gear
Slight article admitted an alternative to double glazing perhaps
Tricky problem to a cook following a Lancashire recipe
It’s wrong, that Carol should stand outside the pub
Comparatively large swallow taken by heads of state
Albert Square’s deserted, unsettled by thunder
In this one may have some perception
